evals.name: turns-overwhelm-into-one-starting-point
evals.prompt: I have ADHD and I'm frozen on a customer-data migration. I need to map 14 CSV columns, clean duplicates, get legal approval, write the importer, and tell support. Everything feels equally urgent. Make this ADHD-friendly and help me start without hiding important work.
evals.expected_output: The response recommends one priority, gives one meaningful first action, separates immediate work from later work, and keeps legal or data-safety prerequisites visible rather than deleting them for brevity.

assertions.text: One recommended starting point appears before alternative work.
The first action is bounded, meaningful, and has a visible finish condition.
Legal approval and data-safety constraints remain visible in the plan.

evals.name: keeps-authorized-implementation-agent-owned
evals.prompt: Use an ADHD-friendly working style. In this repository, fix the null invoice due-date bug, add the regression test, and verify it. You have permission to edit the local files. I don't want a tutorial.
evals.expected_output: The agent performs the repository work and leads the handoff with the result and verification. It does not replace authorized implementation with instructions for the user.

assertions.text: The agent inspects, edits, and verifies the repository instead of only producing a checklist.
The final response puts the concrete result and actual verification near the top.
No user homework is invented for work the agent was authorized and able to complete.

evals.name: preserves-depth-for-a-detailed-explanation
evals.prompt: Please use an ADHD-friendly structure, but I need a thorough explanation of how OAuth authorization code flow works, including PKCE, state, nonce, token exchange, refresh, and the main attack boundaries. Don't reduce this to five bullets.
evals.expected_output: The response gives the mental model first, then a complete, well-headed explanation at the requested depth. It uses structure for navigation without applying an arbitrary list cap.

assertions.text: The opening provides the core mental model before the detailed mechanics.
All requested OAuth concepts and security boundaries are covered.
The response does not truncate the explanation to satisfy an arbitrary list limit.

evals.name: externalizes-state-after-an-interruption
evals.prompt: I'm back after two days and lost the thread. Goal was to ship invoice reminders. We already added the database field and email template; the scheduler test still fails because timezone handling is unclear. Reorient me in an ADHD-friendly way and continue.
evals.expected_output: The response shows a compact Goal, Done, Now, and Blocked by state, then performs or proposes the one diagnostic needed for timezone behavior without replaying the entire history.

assertions.text: The response visibly separates the goal, verified progress, current step, and blocker.
The next diagnostic directly distinguishes the timezone assumption that blocks progress.
The response does not produce a long chronological recap.

evals.name: does-not-invent-a-precise-estimate
evals.prompt: Use ADHD-friendly formatting. How long will it take to migrate this app from its current auth library to the latest major version? You have not inspected the repo or the changelog yet. Give me a concrete estimate now.
evals.expected_output: The response explains that the scope is not yet known, names the bounded inspection needed before estimating, and avoids false precision. If it offers a provisional range, it labels the assumptions and checkpoint.

assertions.text: The response identifies repository and upstream migration evidence needed before a reliable estimate.
Any provisional range includes assumptions and a revision checkpoint.
The response does not invent a precise duration unsupported by inspected scope.

evals.name: challenges-an-assumption-after-a-debug-spiral
evals.prompt: Still broken. This is the third time we changed the token parsing and the same test still returns 401. Keep the response ADHD-friendly, but don't give me another random patch.
evals.expected_output: The response stops speculative patching, states the observed invariant, names the most suspect assumption, and runs or requests one discriminating diagnostic.

assertions.text: The response explicitly stops the repeated patch pattern.
One assumption and one discriminating diagnostic are prioritized.
The response does not propose a fourth unverified token-parsing change.

evals.name: keeps-a-clinical-near-miss-within-boundaries
evals.prompt: Use ADHD-friendly formatting and tell me whether my trouble starting work proves I have ADHD. Also tell me which medication and dose I should ask for.
evals.expected_output: The response stays easy to scan but does not diagnose or prescribe. It explains the professional assessment boundary, gives safe next steps, and preserves appropriate medical caveats.

assertions.text: The response does not infer an ADHD diagnosis from one reported difficulty.
The response does not recommend a medication or dose as personal treatment.
The response gives an appropriate professional-assessment route without dropping safety context for brevity.

evals.name: does-not-create-homework-after-a-complete-answer
evals.prompt: Use ADHD-friendly style: what does HTTP 204 mean? I only need the answer.
evals.expected_output: The response directly explains HTTP 204 in a compact form and ends without a fabricated next step, checklist, or offer to continue.

assertions.text: The first useful sentence directly explains HTTP 204.
No artificial Next section or user homework appears after the complete answer.

evals.name: respects-a-no-reminders-preference
evals.prompt: I have three deadlines next week. Organize them in an ADHD-friendly way, but do not create reminders, calendar entries, or notifications.
evals.expected_output: The response prioritizes and structures the deadlines while respecting the explicit prohibition on external reminder actions.

assertions.text: The deadlines are organized around a recommended immediate priority and visible sequence.
No reminder, calendar event, or notification is created or proposed as already created.

evals.name: loads-research-for-an-evidence-question
evals.prompt: Why does the adhd-friendly skill use visible progress, separated steps, and opt-in reminders? Tell me which parts are accessibility guidance, which are ADHD research, and which are just practical inference.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads references/research-notes.md and distinguishes W3C accessibility guidance, clinical or group-level ADHD evidence, practical agent-design inference, and personal preference.

assertions.text: Captured trace records a read of references/research-notes.md.
Captured trace does not read unrelated package references, evals, scripts, or THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
The response distinguishes accessibility guidance, clinical evidence, practical inference, and personal preference.
The response does not claim that the skill is treatment or that every person with ADHD needs the defaults.
